attempts.summary: Built the lan-a (trusted, node2) / lan-b (guest, node3) topology through node1 (OpenWrt router) using each node's second NIC (node1 eth1↔node2 ens7 for lan-a at 192.168.10.0/24; node1 eth2↔node3 ens7 for lan-b at 192.168.20.0/24), while leaving the original management network (ens2/br-lan) untouched for exec access. Configured OpenWrt firewall zones: 'lana' (trusted, forward=ACCEPT) with an explicit lana->lanb forwarding rule, and 'lanb' (guest, forward=REJECT, input=ACCEPT) so guests reach node1's own services (dnsmasq DNS bound on 192.168.20.1:53) but cannot open any forwarded connection into lan-a. Added static cross-subnet routes on node2/node3 so trusted->guest traffic (allowed) is symmetric. Verified end-to-end: trusted can ping/TCP-connect to guest; guest can query DNS on node1; guest ping/TCP to trusted is rejected by the firewall. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, and node1 (router last), confirming a changed boot marker for each (node2/node3 via boot_id change; node1 via btime/fresh uptime/dmesg since its boot_id string was unexpectedly stable across reboot) and re-verified all UCI config, DNS binding, and the three-way isolation behavior fully recovered after each restart.
